_: The audio pipeline's one table: what to cut, from what, to what.
`npm run audio` reads this, cuts each master with ffmpeg and writes the
encoded file beside it; `npm run build` refuses a stale or over-budget
one through scripts/check-audio.mjs. See docs/audio.md for the argument.
EVERY NUMBER HERE IS THE INPUT, not a record of what happened. The cut
lives in `trim` rather than in a binary somebody has to open, so the
shipped file is reproducible from a committed master and a reviewable
diff. `sourceHash` and `decoded` are the only fields the generator
writes back, and they are what the build gate checks.
The ceiling, in the unit that actually binds. A decoded AudioBuffer is
duration * ctx.sampleRate * channels * 4 bytes and NOTHING else -- the
container, the bitrate and the file's own sample rate are invisible to
it (measured: a 22 kHz file decodes back up to 48 kHz for identical
RAM). So the budget is seconds of mono, not bytes on disk.
44 s = 8 MB at 48 kHz, ~5% of the 157 MB heap FINDINGS.md #1 measures.
A stereo row spends two seconds of it per second of audio.
Cut to the REPORT and nothing after it. The master carries ~865 ms of
baked room -- a flat -18 to -24 dB plateau to 385 ms and then a slow
decay to -68 -- and Sfx already answers every gunshot with a shared
ConvolverNode on a send. Shipping the baked tail would double-reverb
the shot, put one fixed room on six maps, defeat botShot's
distance-climbing send, and hold a voice for 865 ms instead of 150.
Measured before cutting: the report's energy is gone by 130 ms (-8 dB
at 125, -20 by 135), and the 130-400 ms band has a crest factor of
6 dB with no window 5 dB above it -- dense noise, no discrete
reflection and no mechanism, so there is nothing in there to lose.
Stereo, which is the exception to the mono rule rather than a lapse:
the master carries real width (the side channel peaks 10.8 dB under
the mid, so it is not dual-mono), this is the one sample the player
hears UNPANNED as their own report, and at a 150 ms cut the second
channel costs 28 KB. The mono rule earns its keep on long sounds and
on anything only ever heard through a panner.
The only master here that is not one shot. A BURST weapon was recorded
as a burst: the second round arrives at 216 ms at -4 dB and a third
rides its tail out to ~330. `Sfx.shoot` is called once per ROUND, so a
sample carrying the burst would fire nine shots for every three -- this
is cut to the FIRST round and the rest is discarded as a matter of
correctness rather than of taste.
It is also the only master with a LEAD. The report's onset is at 32 ms
and everything before it is -23 to -41 dB of pre-noise; shipped whole
that is 32 ms of latency between the trigger and the sound, which on a
weapon whose three rounds leave 50 ms apart is a third of the burst.
The start sits in the trough at 24 ms (-41 dB) rather than hard against
the onset, so the cut needs no fade in to keep from clicking and the
transient keeps a foot.
96 ms, the shortest cut in the table, and the rate is why: `report.
length` is 0.75 for the same reason ("three of these leave in 0.1 s,
and at the rifle's own length they would run together into a single
ugly shout"). The direct sound is over at 98 ms anyway -- broadband
-9 dB at 96 and -19 by 100.
Cut in the trough between the shot and a discrete second arrival. The
report's high band decays from 124 ms and is 40 dB down by 144; then at
152-172 ms something HF-rich comes back at -8 dB in the band and -15
broadband, which is either a hard slapback or the bolt, and neither
belongs in a sample. `Sfx` answers the first with its own convolver and
the second with `actionPitch`/`actionVol` -- and this weapon's
`actionVol` is 1.55, the highest in the kit, because a blowback SMG is
mostly the sound of its own bolt. Shipping the recorded one would play
that mechanism twice.
140 ms against a 77 ms gap at 13 rounds a second, so two rounds always
overlap -- the same ratio the rifle already ships (150 ms on a 106 ms
gap), and the fade lands on the cliff rather than on the next round.
The longest cut in the table, and the master earns it rather than the
weapon being indulged: the high band stays live -- between -9 and -20 dB
-- all the way to 156 ms, drops to -26 at 160 and PLATEAUS there for the
next 60. A plateau in the high band is a room's early field; a decay is
a shot. So the direct sound genuinely runs to ~158 and the fade covers
the handover exactly.
What is discarded past it is that plateau out to 220 ms and then a
discrete late arrival at 224-232 (-10 dB broadband, 30 dB down in the
high band) -- a reflection off something a good way off, and the single
clearest case in these six of a room that is not this game's. At 3
rounds a second 180 ms is barely half the gap, so nothing here is
spent against the next round.
The one master with NO cliff in it, which is why this row's fade is
nearly a third of its length instead of the 15 ms every other row uses.
The rifle's cut could land on a 15 dB step at 130 ms and hide there;
this file is still only 6 dB down at 296 ms and its decay does not
become a straight line in dB until ~400. There is no moment to cut on,
so the cut has to be MADE, and a fade is the honest way to make one.
Where it goes is the high band. The crack is over by ~90 ms; from 95 ms
the band sits at -21 dB +/-2 for the next hundred milliseconds, which is
a dense early field rather than anything the weapon did, and at 200-212
a discrete arrival comes back at -9. So the shot is 0-90 and the fade
spends 90-130 handing it to `Sfx`'s convolver.
It is also the widest master in the set -- the side channel peaks only
3.8 dB under the mid, against the assault rifle's 10.8 -- which is the
room again, and another reason not to ship much of it: one recorded
room heard in stereo is the same fixed room on six maps that the
assault rifle's row argues against, only more audibly.
The second master with a lead, and the longest: 50 ms of it, -27 to
-57 dB, before the report starts at 52. Same rule as the burst rifle --
shipped whole it is 50 ms of trigger latency on a weapon that fires
every 100 -- and the same placement, in the trough at 40 ms (-50 dB)
rather than hard against the onset.
The end is where the high band stops decaying and the low band does
not. Above 4 kHz the shot falls from -7 dB at 116 ms to -33 at 140 and
-55 by 180, a clean exponential decay; broadband it is still -13 at 180
because what is left is low roll, and the 300-500 ms band measures a
crest factor of 2.6 to 3.8 dB, which is undiluted noise. That low roll
is exactly what `report.weight` and `length` are for, so the cut takes
the direct sound to ~140 and fades the rest out over the next 30.
The cleanest of the six and the closest in shape to the assault rifle's:
a report to ~100 ms and then a 20 dB collapse over the next 25. The one
thing inside it worth naming is the high-band spike at 84-92 ms, which
is the slide -- kept, because it is inside the report and the assault
rifle's own cut keeps the same event at 126 ms, and because the fade is
already running by the time it would have to be argued about.
What is dropped is a floor at -28 to -38 dB from 130 ms and then a late
arrival at 220-240 that climbs back to -21, which is the room.
The cupola gun on all three hulls, and the FIRST MONO ROW in this table.
Every other row is stereo under the exception docs/audio.md grants a
short sound the player hears UNPANNED as their own report; this one has
no such claim. `Game.resolveMg` reaches `Sfx.botShot` and not `shoot`,
deliberately -- the gun is twelve metres from the listener in a chase
view -- so a PannerNode makes the stereo and a second channel would be
double the RAM for nothing. It costs 0.112 mono-seconds where a stereo
cut of the same length would cost 0.224.
The THIRD master to lead with its mechanism, and the plainest of them: a
discrete clack at 8-16 ms (-6 dB in the band above 4 kHz), then near
silence to -61, then the report at 40. Cut at 34 ms, in that trough. The
clack is a feed or a bolt and `actionPitch`/`actionVol` on the three mg
rows are what voice it, as on every other row here.
The end is the rate. The report is over at ~126 ms -- broadband -11 at
124 and -19 by 128, with the band above 4 kHz decaying from -21 -- and
what follows is low roll the room is holding, at -10 to -18 broadband
with that band 24 to 36 dB down, plus a discrete arrival at 148. The cut
is 112 ms, which is the tank's own 111 ms gap at fireRate 9 to within a
millisecond: one round is done when the next one leaves, no two stack,
and that is the same claim `report.length` of 0.72 already makes for this
gun ("almost no ring, because the next one is 110 ms away"). The truck's
133 ms and the helicopter's 118 are looser still.
